invariants: No SQL executes outside the owner-scoped transaction, including the readiness probe.
A call that fails because the connection broke surfaces as AdapterError::Unavailable (via the From impl: err.is_closed()); the session is then dead and is never silently reconnected.
PgSession is not Sync and is never shared: one session, one connection, one thread.
This module has NO #[cfg(test)] module: it contains no pure logic, and unit tests must never touch a live database. Behavior is covered by live smoke checks outside cargo test.

tokio-postgres API facts (do not invent alternatives): tokio_postgres::Config::connect(NoTls) is async and returns (Client, Connection); Client::transaction(&mut self) is async; Transaction has query_one, query_opt, execute, batch_execute and commit, all async; there is no Client::connect associated function and no set_statement_timeout method.
responsibilities: Own the PgConfig, a tokio multi-thread Runtime (2 workers), and the tokio_postgres Client; all fields private.

connect(): validate the config, build the runtime with tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread().enable_all(), then rt.block_on the async connect: cfg.connect(tokio_postgres::NoTls) returns (client, connection); spawn the connection future onto the runtime; apply the statement timeout with client.batch_execute of a SET statement_timeout built from the config's whole seconds; then prove readiness by running the same owner-scoped transaction path as every call with select "SELECT 1".

Every call_* body is one rt.block_on(async { ... }) over &mut self.client with exactly these steps: let mut tx = client.transaction().await?; tx.batch_execute or execute of SELECT set_config('forge.coding_owner', '<owner>', true) with the owner bound as a parameter; run the query ON THE TRANSACTION (tx.query_one / tx.query_opt with the caller's select string and params); tx.commit().await?. Dropping tx uncommitted rolls back.

call_scalar uses tx.query_opt and maps the row with row.get(0); call_json/call_bool/call_text use tx.query_one and row.get(0) (call_bool unwraps its bool via row.get::<usize, bool>(0) after query_one on a query known to return one row); call_void uses tx.execute and discards the count.
Errors from tokio-postgres map through the From<tokio_postgres::Error> impl in error.rs (the ? operator) - never map them to Protocol by hand.

in_tx(f): run the closure inside ONE owner-scoped transaction - the run_query envelope generalized from one statement to a closure: open client.transaction(), execute the owner set_config, build a crate::tx::Tx over the transaction plus the runtime handle, run f via tokio::task::block_in_place (the closure's Tx calls block_on the handle), then commit; any error drops the transaction uncommitted (rollback).
summary: One adapter session: a tokio-postgres client behind a synchronous facade, and the owner-scoped transaction every call runs in.
